Start by researchin...
item.description:
@undefined

Now that you've learned automation, here's a practical idea you can explore: Start by researching the top 20 niches in vertical SaaS, what many call the "boring businesses" (e.g., laundromats, locksmiths, dental clinics, etc.). Next, head to ChatGPT or Grok and use this prompt: 1. "What are some complex and repetitive tasks that business owners in [insert niche, e.g., laundromat or locksmith] deal with regularly?" Wait for the output and analyze the answers. Then use this follow-up prompt: 2. "Create a simple SOP in Notion that automates the tasks mentioned above using Zapier or Make. com. Make it beginner-friendly and include step-by-step visuals and explanations." Once you have this system documented: 3. Identify and build a list of at least 300 business owners in that niche. 4. Package the SOP into a well-designed PDF and share it with them (via email or DMs). 5. Offer an upsell by helping them implement or customize the system. Here's a sample cold outreach message you can use: Subject: Want to automate your customer follow-ups? Hey Akin, I noticed you're doing great with your laundromat business. I recently built an AI-powered automation system that completely handles invoicing and customer follow-ups. No manual input or human intervention required. Would you be open to seeing a quick demo?

item.title: Trends that are shaping Web2 (and some are spilling over to Web3) ​ -Web2 AI-native companies get...
item.description:
@undefined

Trends that are shaping Web2 (and some are spilling over to Web3) ​ -Web2 AI-native companies get their product to market much quicker than before through the help of GenAI tools and coding co-pilot. Many reach $1M ARR much faster than the SaaS counterpart at 8-9 months vs 13+ months ​ Faster product cycle -> faster GTM -> faster PMF ​ -Over ~80% of AI-native builders are investing AI agents or autonomous systems designed to take multi-step actions on behalf of users and 65% focus on Vertical AI applications targeting specific niche/sector. ​ AI Agents will eliminate the need to interact with websites, applications, interfaces ​ -Almost 90% of YC startups in 2025 are AI-native startups, up from ~20% pre-GPT era and the trend is likely going to continue from here. ​ AI converges across all sectors ​ -Pricing model shifted from purely subscription model to a combination of freemium (basic features) + subscription + usage-based pricing + outcome-based. Many opt for a hybrid model between subscription & usage-based to cater to different types of users. ​ Sharper pricing, catering to the demand of users ​ -Big enterprises are allocating bigger AI budget from ~5% before 2024 to 10-20% in 2025. ​ Bigger AI spend from enterprises translate to bigger ARPU for AI-native startups Web3 AI is ~6 months behind Web2 AI but for financial use cases & autonomous agent systems for trading & prediction, Web3 AI is making rapid progress. Watch out for (i) Web3-native workflows / agents with sticky product (ii) Scalable & modular agent-to-agent system (iii) Trading & prediction agents powered by evolving AI/ML systems (iv) Teams with pricing model that leverage token as growth lever, enhancing subscription/usage-based model (v) Unique adoption & application of AI on new Web3 verticals (vi) Web3-native co-pilots accelerating smart contracts development & Defi/AI deployment

So serve established platforms user-base, scale your AI solution to decent MRR and sell it for 8 figs in 2 years. This is the easiest way to build a profitable B2B SaaS with AI Tech. For ex: I'm building @CodeGuidedev with a vision in mind and after I made some revenue numbers public I'm getting 5-8 emails from VCs and Private equity forms every week to either invest in CodeGuide or to acquire it. And I'm talking 8-figs here. If I were to start again, I would not start building something from scratch. But as @karpathy explained, I would start with partial autonomy (embed AI into existing platforms). I hope this helps.
